sources.note: Features coded: 10A (from Wang-and-Zheng-1993), 41A, 42A (p. 52), 70A, 71A (p. 37), 72A (pp. 100-101), 110A, 111A (pp. 85-86). No stress features (14A/15A) coded for Mulam.

sources.citation: Coyaud, Maurice (1987). Les langues dans le monde chinois. Paris: P.A.F. (Pour l'Analyse du Folklore). Section 3.43 'Le mulao', p. 131 (Rosetta Project one-page extract, plus table of contents and bibliography pp. 205-207).
sources.note: Nothing. The page gives the initial and final inventories and the tone system only: 'TONS : six tons en syllabe ouverte, et deux en syllabe fermee, ou l'opposition de longueur est pertinente. Ton 1 : 42... Ton 8 long: 11 pa:k "grelon"'. It states it is based on Wang Jun (1980). No word on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Mulam language' (citing Wang Jun & Zheng Guoqiao 1980, Mulao yu jianzhi).
sources.note: 'a tonal language with ten tones'; eleven vowels; voiceless/voiced nasals and laterals. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (zh), '仫佬语'.
sources.note: Only notes voiceless/voiced nasal and lateral initials and two palatalization series; nothing on tones or stress.

sources.note: Bibliography only. Descriptive refs: Yin Shage 2014 grammar (7+445 pp., Chinese) and 2012 dissertation; Wang & Zheng 1980 (Chinese, 119/125 pp.) and its 1993 English translation (vi+132 pp., ANU National Thai Studies Centre, ISBN 073151551X, OCLC 29971737); Yue Jing 2004 Minzu Yuwen sketch; Deng Li 2021 MA thesis on Mulam phonetics under Chinese contact; Zheng Guoqiao 1988 'The influences of Han on the Mulam language' in Comparative Kadai (SIL 86); Benedict 1983 'Mulao: key to Kadai phonology'. Bo Wenze 2003 'Mulao yu yanjiu' is the Guizhou Mulao [giu, gela1264], a different language.
